core_obligations: Existence over an affine base (proof lines 5584-5620): choose an affine open covering of the source, compose the given morphism with the localization morphisms attached to the inclusions, apply the affine case to each piece, and glue the resulting morphisms of schemes using the uniqueness statement.

Global existence (proof lines 5620-5688): cover the target by affine opens, apply the previous paragraph to the restrictions, and use uniqueness of the local morphisms to see that the morphisms obtained for varying affine opens agree on overlaps, producing a global morphism of schemes.

The 2-isomorphism and uniqueness (proof lines 5688-5693): the 2-isomorphisms supplied by the affine case are compatible on overlaps by the rigidity lemma, giving a global 2-isomorphism from the morphism of topoi to the one attached to the morphism of schemes; uniqueness then follows from the same rigidity.
proof_roadmap: Prove existence when the target is affine by gluing the local construction over an affine open covering of the source.
Pass to an arbitrary target by covering it by affine opens and matching the local morphisms on overlaps.
Upgrade the morphisms to a 2-isomorphism using rigidity, which also gives uniqueness.
difficulty_reason: The theorem is the fully faithfulness statement that the construction sending a scheme to its small etale topos with structure sheaf is fully faithful: every morphism of locally ringed topoi comes from a unique morphism of schemes, up to a 2-isomorphism (statement lines 5552-5571). The proof is a long gluing argument: the author first treats the case of an affine target, composing with localization morphisms and applying the affine case over an affine open covering of the source (proof lines 5584-5620); then covers the target by affine opens and observes that the local morphisms agree on overlaps by rigidity, producing a global morphism of schemes (proof lines 5620-5688); finally the 2-isomorphisms are glued by the same rigidity and uniqueness is recorded (proof lines 5688-5693). The non-formal content is the gluing both of the morphisms and of the 2-isomorphisms. The claim is H2: a structured construction carried out in two stages with the rigidity input named.
